record.paper_title: Open Questions in Charm Decays Deserving an Answer
record.original_question: What are the branching fractions for the radiative and rare charm decays D -> gamma K^*, D -> gamma rho/omega, D_s -> gamma phi, D_s -> gamma rho/omega, and related D -> l^+ l^- K/K^*/rho/omega modes, and does the ratio BR(D -> gamma rho/omega)/BR(D -> gamma K^*) differ from tan^2 theta_c in a way that would signal New Physics in c -> u gamma rather than ordinary weak-annihilation dynamics?

evidence.quote: Measuring BR(D → γK∗ ) and BR(D → γρ/ω) will provide us with an important calibration for gauging the impact of WA on B → γρ/ω. As a rough estimate one expects BR(D → γK∗ ) ∼ 10−5 − 10−4 and BR(D → γρ/ω) ∼ 10−6 − 10−5 [8].
Observing BR(D → γρ/ω) / BR(D → γK∗ ) 6= tan2 θc (5) would then signal the intervention of NP, of which non-minimal SUSY is one relevant example [9]!

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the radiative and rare charm-meson decays
  D → γ K*,  D → γ ρ/ω,  D_s → γ φ,  D_s → γ ρ/ω,
together with the related rare leptonic-pair modes
  D → ℓ⁺ℓ⁻ K,  D → ℓ⁺ℓ⁻ K*,  D → ℓ⁺ℓ⁻ ρ,  D → ℓ⁺ℓ⁻ ω,
where ℓ ∈ {e, μ}. Let θ_c denote the Cabibbo angle, so that tan²θ_c ≈ 0.05.

(a) Determine the Standard-Model branching fractions of each of the above decay modes, including a reliable theoretical treatment of long-distance contributions (in particular weak-annihilation/exchange dynamics) and short-distance c → u γ and c → u ℓ⁺ℓ⁻ amplitudes.

(b) Predict the ratio
  R := BR(D → γ ρ/ω) / BR(D → γ K*)
within the Standard Model, and establish quantitatively whether, and by how much, the inequality R ≠ tan²θ_c can arise from ordinary weak-annihilation dynamics alone, versus serving as a clean signal of New Physics (for example non-minimal supersymmetric contributions) entering c → u γ. Identify the threshold of deviation of R from tan²θ_c above which a New-Physics interpretation becomes unavoidable.
artifact.status_search_result: Several of the branching fractions have been measured: BaBar measured BR(D⁰ → K̄*⁰γ) and BR(D⁰ → φγ) (Phys. Rev. D 78, 071101, 2008), and Belle observed D⁰ → ρ⁰γ with BR ≈ 1.77×10⁻⁵ (Phys. Rev. Lett. 118, 051801, 2017). However, robust Standard-Model predictions for the radiative modes are still hampered by large long-distance/weak-annihilation uncertainties (see e.g. JHEP 08 (2017) 091, "Rare radiative charm decays within the SM and beyond"), so the clean separation of New Physics in c → u γ from weak-annihilation dynamics via the ratio R = BR(D → γρ/ω)/BR(D → γK*) remains unresolved. Several of the rare D → ℓ⁺ℓ⁻ (K,K*,ρ,ω) modes have not yet been observed. Thus the program is partially completed.

status_evidence.title: Measurement of the Branching Fractions of the Radiative Charm Decays (BaBar)
status_evidence.snippet: BR(D⁰ → K̄*⁰γ)/BR(D⁰ → K⁻π⁺) = (8.43 ± 0.51 ± 0.70)×10⁻³; first measurement of D⁰ → K̄*⁰γ.

status_evidence.title: Observation of D⁰ → ρ⁰γ and Search for CP Violation in Radiative Charm Decays (Belle)
status_evidence.snippet: First observation of D⁰ → ρ⁰γ with BR = (1.77 ± 0.30 ± 0.07)×10⁻⁵.

status_evidence.title: Rare radiative charm decays within the Standard Model and beyond
status_evidence.snippet: Theoretical study of c → uγ noting large long-distance contributions and discussing NP sensitivity in radiative charm decays.
status_evidence.claim: Disentangling NP from weak-annihilation dynamics in c → uγ remains theoretically challenging.
